top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) solved a distinct elementary-step problem from the 2010 C-C coupling prize: amine binding, deprotonation and difficult C-N reductive elimination against beta-hydride elimination and catalyst deactivation. The ligand-design and mechanistic solution is general, independently confirmed for about thirty years, and routine in medicinal and process chemistry. The allocation is a clean pair with a short citation. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (P002) are scientifically strong but have a three-name allocation among six credited and a closer link to the 2023 Medicine prize, so I rank them second, above no award.
